question: In the context of Indian satellite launch vehicle, how many stages did GSLV-D1 has?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Three**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle (GSLV-D1)** is a three-stage launch vehicle designed and operated by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)** for launching satellites into geostationary orbits.
 
• The three stages of the GSLV-D1 are as follows:
 
 
• **First Stage (Solid Booster Stage):** This stage uses a solid rocket motor called S125/S139 and is augmented by four liquid strap-on boosters (L40).
 
• **Second Stage (Liquid Core Stage):** This stage is powered by the Vikas engine, which uses liquid propellant for propulsion.
 
• **Third Stage (Cryogenic Upper Stage):** This stage uses a cryogenic engine that burns liquid hydrogen (LH2) and liquid oxygen (LOX) as propellants. It is crucial for placing satellites into geostationary transfer orbits (GTO).
 
 
 
• GSLV-D1 was the **first developmental flight** of the GSLV series and was launched on **April 18, 2001**, from the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC)**, Sriharikota.
